effect_mechanism: Restoring forest on degraded land rebuilds habitat: a global meta-analysis of 221 study landscapes found forest restoration enhances biodiversity by 15-84% compared with degraded ecosystems [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1], natural regeneration outperformed active planting for plants, birds and invertebrates by 34 to 56% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], and restored mangroves support more crab production and diversity than degraded mangroves [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_1]. In the western Andes of Colombia, bird and dung beetle communities in regenerating forest resembled old growth after 15-30 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1]; protecting and managing existing forest retains habitat, with community forest management in Nepal reducing deforestation and forest cover in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla rising 8% [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan and Turkmenistan rate diversity as increased. In Senegal's southern Groundnut Basin woody species richness rose from 27 species in a 1-year exclosure to 51 species in 5- and 12-year exclosures [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
conditionality: Recovery is partial and slow: after 20 years of natural regeneration species richness reached 78% of old-growth values but composition only 33%, with recovery of composition taking about 120 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_2], and in Brazil's Atlantic Forest regaining mature-forest endemism was estimated to take 1987 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. The forest-cover units are a component proxy and the low-income evidence is largely compiler ratings. Governance effects are uneven: under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

conditionality: Recovery of the full community is slow: the Atlantic Forest chronosequence estimates 65 years to reach 80% animal-dispersed species and 1987 years to regain mature-forest endemism [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. The Thai case has no unplanted control, the Mexican forest-cover gain is a before-after comparison without a counterfactual and enters as a component proxy, and the Colombian result is cited from another study. In Vietnam an evaluation of grants to special-use forest management boards found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that biodiversity is hard to assess and the tracking tool used was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1].

effect_mechanism: Natural regeneration rebuilds biodiversity as secondary forest develops. Across tropical chronosequences species richness recovers fastest and composition slowest, with richness after 20 years at 78% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_2]; tree species richness in Brazil's Atlantic Forest rises with time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1]; and in the western Andes of Colombia bird and dung beetle communities in regenerating forest came to resemble old growth [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1]. A pantropical meta-analysis finds natural regeneration outperforms active planting for plants, birds and invertebrates [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], an Ethiopian WOCAT compiler rates animal diversity as increased under area closure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity], and in Senegal's southern Groundnut Basin woody species richness in exclosures rose from 27 species after 1 year to 51 species after 5 and 12 years, an increase of more than 52% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].
conditionality: Recovery of composition and endemism is slow: composition after 20 years was only 33% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1], and in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest regaining mature-forest endemism was estimated to take 1987 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. A French review citing a global analysis reports species richness losses after clear-cutting followed by natural regeneration relative to uncut forest, though smaller than under plantations [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_3], the meta-analysis compares regeneration with planting rather than with degraded land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], and the Ethiopian compiler notes that returning wildlife damages crops and livestock [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The Senegal result compares exclosures of different ages at one site rather than exclosures with open grazed land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].

effect_mechanism: Restoration accumulates carbon in regrowing biomass and soils: natural regeneration removes 9.1-18.8 t CO2/ha/yr in its first 20 years and planted mangroves up to 23.1 [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_3, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_2], a 20-year-old secondary forest in the moist tropics holds 51 t of above-ground carbon per hectare on average [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch19_1], and modelled 30-year carbon is higher for natural regeneration (60.2 tC/ha) than for harvested plantations (44.6 tC/ha) [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. Restored mangroves sequester more carbon than unvegetated tidal flats [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1], sustainable forest management sites under GEF projects sequester about 1.33 t of carbon per hectare per year more than the counterfactual [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1], and secondary regrowth in the central Amazon of Brazil reached 50% of mature forest biomass after 25 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_gehring05_1]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: Biomass recovery is slow (about 12 decades to reach 90% of old-growth above-ground biomass) even though topsoil carbon recovers in about 5 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_poorter21_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_poorter21_1]. Afforestation soil carbon gains were not significant on pastures and grasslands and boreal sites lost 1.5% [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4], community management in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1], the modelled estimates are discounted present values or scenario potentials, and planted-forest removal factors include commercial woodlots. Soil carbon and forest cover enter as component proxies, and the low-income evidence is mostly compiler ratings. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

effect_mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

effect_mechanism: Reforestation slows storm runoff and lowers flood peaks in catchment models: in Slovakia's Hornad watershed a 50% increase of forest cut a simulated flood peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and reduced peaks by about 24% on average in rain-duration tests, more for short storms than long ones [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and an afforestation simulation for Luxembourg's Alzette basin decreased the peak by 8% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. A systematic review found that flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of studies reporting them [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde, Uganda and Bosnia and Herzegovina, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan, mangrove buffers in the Philippines, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and a learning site in Afghanistan rate downstream flooding or flood impacts as reduced; an Ethiopian compiler notes that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced, and the Afghan compiler that riverbanks were revegetated with communities planting cuttings along banks and shorelines [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
conditionality: The modelled benefit shrinks as rain continues, from 29% for the shortest rain duration to 17% for the longest [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and all catchment results are scenarios of large forest-cover gains in temperate high-income basins; the largest figure, a 42.3% peak reduction from converting all arable land to forest, is a secondary citation with no basin named [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The Honduras compiler rates no downstream change yet, expecting reforestation to reduce floods in the lower river only in the long term, and the Bangladesh and Bosnia and Herzegovina compilers rate only a slight reduction [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_downstream_flooding]. The review pools restoration with forestry and afforestation and reports vote counts rather than magnitudes [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1], and the low- and middle-income evidence consists of WOCAT compiler ratings, not measured flows or flood damage. Expert syntheses dispute that planting at scale reduces floods: an FAO–CIFOR review concludes that massive programmes of forestation proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may have many other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a comment on a global flood analysis argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding, for example if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change, and settlements, roads and drains remain unaltered [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. Both are expert positions rather than measurements, the FAO–CIFOR statement citing earlier work.

effect_mechanism: Mangrove belts lower coastal flood impact by attenuating wind waves and, far more weakly, storm-surge water levels as water passes through the forest, with attenuation depending on inundation depth, tree species, density and creeks. A global flood model finds that losing current mangroves would increase the land, people and property flooded each year, and in Orissa, India, villages behind mangroves had fewer cyclone deaths and lower household losses; WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased. In Bangladesh, a cited model finds 500 m mangrove afforestation patches can mitigate surge current velocities by up to 90% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2].
conditionality: Almost all measured and modelled evidence concerns existing mangrove forests rather than restored stands, so the transfer to restoration is assumed. Measured surge reductions come from south Florida in the USA, wave reductions are upper bounds partly derived from small-wave measurements, and the Orissa household-loss comparison is a perception-based survey of a few villages. The Bangladesh study is modelled grey literature from the World Bank, and it finds mangroves have only a small effect (<4%) on design total water level because the surge dominates, so their benefit there is protection of embankments from erosion and currents rather than lower flood levels [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2].

effect_mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases, community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]; in Costa Rica, payments for reforestation made up 18.66% of participants' income, against about 10% of family income in other Latin American programmes [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Mangrove planting in Viet Nam raised shell and oyster yields per hectare, with benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits, and a global meta-analysis gives mangrove restoration benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_su21_1]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes, and plantations would be profitable without carbon payments across 28.3% of the plantation-feasible area [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2, ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, the Ugandan compiler rates it unchanged, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, an implementer-commissioned evaluation in Viet Nam, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), perception scores (the Costa Rica economic impact of 63.9%), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2, ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_padilla17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Vietnam's plantation return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and its gains rested on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1], Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group.

effect_mechanism: Mangrove planting supports coastal livelihoods mainly through aquatic products: in northern Viet Nam the community mangrove plantation project raised per-hectare yields of shells and oysters and so local income, and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives benefit-cost ratios above unity in every commune, higher when ecological benefits are counted. A global meta-analysis likewise finds mangrove restoration benefits exceed costs, a cited Philippine study concludes the same, and WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and Senegal rate food self-sufficiency, production risk and long-term returns as improved. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD/ha, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD/ha [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Valuations of standing mangroves show what keeping them is worth to coastal households: in Orissa, India, existing mangroves provided house-protection benefits of USD 1218 per hectare in a single super cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], a comparison of costs and benefits found protecting the remaining mangroves there economically justified [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1], and in Thailand storm protection accounted for US$ 8,966–10,821 per hectare (~87%) of estimated mangrove value, with the long-term total economic value of an intact mangrove swamp about 3.6 times that of converting it to shrimp aquaculture [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2].
conditionality: The Viet Nam figures come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model benefits forward and include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples. Poverty is reached only through proxies (economic return, food security, income), and the WOCAT entries are compiler ratings. The Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed household income, and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The protection value alone does not always win: in Orissa the value of coastal land in alternate uses far exceeds the value mangroves provide by protecting residential property, so on that basis alone conservation or rehabilitation could not be justified [ev_economic_return_das11_2], and the government's early warning saved more lives than mangroves did [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1]. These valuations concern existing mangroves rather than restored stands, and the Thai figures are model estimates cited in a review [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2].

effect_mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income, employment and food from forests. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases [ev_household_income_iufro20_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. effect_mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent, tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce landslide risk, eucalyptus afforestation plots in Calabria, Italy with good canopy gave lower sediment concentrations than plots with little or no tree cover, and China's reforestation programmes reduced soil erosion and sediments [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa and Asia widely rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased under planting, regeneration and area closure, citing vegetation cover, sediment held upstream and slower flows [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. A World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].

The Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion, most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, several sheets bundle planting with structures such as bunds or terraces, the measured plot and model evidence is mostly from high-income temperate settings, and the runoff results (including the Ethiopian runoff coefficients) measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. effect_mechanism: This row describes the slope stability that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: landslides begin to increase when roots decay at around three years after forest clearance and susceptibility remains high until around 15 years, rates of mass erosion on steep forested terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after timber harvesting, and in southeast Alaska the area affected by landslides after logging was 5 times greater than in a 100-year period before it [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis likewise notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil a certain amount of mechanical support, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The landslide units are forest-loss contrasts and expert consensus, largely from temperate regions and cited second-hand, so they show what clearing costs rather than measuring the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. The root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by the presence or absence of a well-developed forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. A measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1].

conditionality: Agreement is mixed and the measured evidence often points the other way: in the same review annual water yield decreased in about 80% of study cases after forest restoration or cover expansion, baseflow in 63% and groundwater levels or recharge in 67% [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1, ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1]; native-species plantations aged 25 to 45 years in the US Pacific Northwest produce dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to old growth, afforestation in New Zealand reduces water yield, and some modelled regions show nonsignificant declines [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3, ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4, ev_water_regulation_teo22_5].
